run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application in namespace hotel-reservation was freshly rolled out at ~10:01:50Z and load-tested by a wrk2 pod (http://10.96.112.199:5000, the frontend Service) from 10:02:09Z to 10:04:12Z. All 19 deployments report 1/1 available and all pods are Running with 0 restarts, no container waiting reasons and no CPU throttling. No application-level failure is observable: no error log lines in any hotel-reservation service pod during the traffic period, the sampled frontend spans all recorded http.status_code=200 with sub-10 ms durations, no span anywhere exceeds 10 ms, and the search/rate application metrics show search_rate_failures_total=0 and search_rate_timeouts_total=0 against 4330 attempts/successes with rate_queue_depth=0, rate_in_flight=0, no rejected and no expired requests. The only fault material in the environment is a pair of ConfigMaps, failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, holding scripts that drop the MongoDB `admin` user or revoke its readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db (plus mitigation scripts); both are mounted at /scripts in the current (revision 2) ReplicaSets of mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate, which replaced their revision-1 ReplicaSets at ~10:01:51-55Z. Both mongod init scripts completed and granted readWrite to `admin` at 10:01:59-10:02:00Z, and every observed `admin` login succeeds, so the user was not dropped. I could not observe the injection itself, and no scenario-visible impact is present. The leading hypothesis is a revocation of the `admin` readWrite privilege on geo-db: it is the only candidate that cannot be falsified by the observed traffic, because the geo service never issues a query to geo-db at request time (all 4186 /geo.Geo/Nearby spans are <=1 ms, mean 0.102 ms, and mongodb-geo has the lowest CPU of all six mongod pods, 0.00123 cores), so such a revocation would silently degrade geo results instead of raising errors. The equivalent rate-db hypothesis is contradicted for 10:02:24-10:03:25Z: the three rate-to-mongo accesses in that period re-authenticated as `admin` and all 4330 search->rate calls succeeded with zero failures and timeouts. One client-side symptom remains unexplained: wrk2 reports 194/187/183/192 socket timeouts per 30 s round (~6%) with 0 connect/read/write errors and no 'Non-2xx' responses, while every recorded server span is under 10 ms - requests that apparently never produced a response. I could not attribute it to any service. Decoys checked and set aside: the audit-log-archiver CronJob pods are not-ready only because the archiver container exits after completing its transfer; whether the failing blackbox ingress probe reflects a real misconfiguration is unresolved, since the query for Ingress objects returned no data and only direct service probes were observed healthy.

claims.text: All 19 deployments in hotel-reservation report 1 ready/1 available replica, and all 21 pods in the namespace are phase Running with restart counts of 0 (the audit-log-archiver pods show ready=false only for the short-lived archiver container).

ConfigMap failure-admin-geo (hotel-reservation) contains remove-admin-mongo.sh (db.dropUser('admin')), revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh (db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'geo-db'}])) and their mitigation scripts; ConfigMap failure-admin-rate contains the same set targeting rate-db.

The fault ConfigMaps were created at 2026-11-21T10:01:51Z together with the rest of the application release (mongo-geo-script at 10:01:50Z, mongo-rate-script at 10:01:50Z), i.e. they are part of the deployed manifests rather than a later edit; failure-admin-geo has resourceVersion 58962 and failure-admin-rate 58961.

The current ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 (deployment revision 2, 1 replica each) mount ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate at /scripts next to /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d, while the scaled-to-zero revision-1 ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf do not mount that volume.

Warning events at 10:01:54Z show the superseded pods mongodb-geo-78487c9767-wxhdd and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-7ftmq disappearing during volume binding (FailedScheduling: pod does not exist any more), i.e. mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate were rolled to the new revision at ~10:01:51-55Z.

The mongod init scripts completed on both databases and logged 'Granting readWrite role to admin on geo-db database...' (10:01:59.842Z) and 'Granting readWrite role to admin on rate-db database...' (10:01:59.934Z) followed by 'Initialization script completed', with no error output.
mongodb-geo logs admin authentication success and creation of collection geo-db.geo with indexes at 10:02:02Z, so the admin user existed with readWrite rights on geo-db at that moment.

mongodb-rate logs 'Authentication succeeded' for principalName=admin on connection conn6 at 10:02:24.648Z, 10:02:42.466Z and 10:03:25.396Z - i.e. the admin user still existed and authenticated in that period.

Application metrics from search.hotel-reservation:9092 show search_rate_attempts_total == search_rate_successes_total == search_requests_total == 4330 with search_rate_failures_total = 0 and search_rate_timeouts_total = 0, and from rate.hotel-reservation:9091 rate_requests_received_total == rate_requests_completed_total == 3574 with rate_requests_rejected_total = 0, rate_requests_expired_total = 0, rate_queue_depth = 0, rate_in_flight = 0 (rate_backend_qps_limit 500, rate_queue_capacity 256).

Every geo service span is below 1 ms: for the 25-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, service_name=geo has le=1 cumulative value 4186.368 equal to its +Inf total 4186.368 (frontend, by contrast, has 19537 of 25223 spans <=2.5 ms and 24087 <=5 ms), and the geo /geo.Geo/Nearby mean duration was 0.1018 ms.

mongodb-geo had the lowest CPU of all six mongod pods in the namespace (0.00123 cores over 5m), below mongodb-user (0.00132), mongodb-rate (0.00157), mongodb-profile (0.00180), mongodb-recommendation (0.00193) and mongodb-reservation (0.00240), consistent with geo-db not serving per-request reads.

Sampled frontend spans for HTTP GET /hotels, HTTP GET /recommendations and HTTP POST /reservation all carry http.status_code=200 with durations of 2-10 ms (e.g. /hotels 2.9-5.3 ms, POST /reservation 5.6-10.2 ms); no span in the sample has an error status tag.

The wrk2 load generator completed four 30 s rounds inside the window (2971, 2934, 2973 and 2972 requests; 98.91, 97.78, 98.99 and 98.95 requests/sec) each reporting 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 194/187/183/192' and recorded a maximum latency of only ~15 ms; a Loki query over its log for 'Non-2xx|Requests/sec|requests in|Socket errors|Running wrk2|Latency|thread' returned 29 lines containing the round summaries but no non-2xx response line.

No error, failure, deadline, EOF or refusal lines appear in the logs of frontend, search, rate, reservation, profile, recommendation or user between 10:02:00Z and 10:04:17Z (the query returned only two benign tuning lines), and the namespace-wide error-style query returned only wrk2 socket-timeout lines plus frontend->consul 'connection refused' lines from 10:01:53-54Z at startup.

No container in hotel-reservation was CPU-throttled in the window (throttled/periods ratio 0 for consul, frontend, geo, jaeger, memcached, mongodb-reservation, profile, recommendation, search and user), and frontend working-set memory was flat (10.7 MB at 10:03 and 10.68 MB at 10:04).

The only firing/pending alerts concern volume, not errors: HighRequestRate is pending for frontend (191.4 req/s), profile (105.1), reservation (95.7), search (95.1) and rate (63.4), KubePodNotReady is pending for audit-log-archiver-29920923-j8rtm, while HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, DeploymentNotReady, ContainerCPUThrottling and HTTPProbeFailure are inactive.

The equivalent fault on rate-db is contradicted for 10:02:24-10:03:25Z: rate's three mongo accesses in that period re-authenticated successfully as admin, the mongo_rate client-span mean was 7.32 ms (not an immediate authorization rejection), and all 4330 search->rate attempts succeeded with search_rate_failures_total=0 and search_rate_timeouts_total=0.

The 'remove admin user' variant (remove-admin-mongo.sh, db.dropUser('admin')) was rejected: both mongod pods log successful authentication of principalName=admin after startup (mongodb-geo 10:02:02Z, mongodb-rate 10:02:24/10:02:42/10:03:25Z), so the admin user was not dropped.

The not-ready audit-log-archiver pod (KubePodNotReady pending for audit-log-archiver-29920923-j8rtm) is not the incident: its archiver container logs 'audit record forwarded' and 'upload complete (0 bytes archived)' and then simply exits, which is the normal completion of the CronJob shell script, and its fluent-bit sidecar keeps running.

The failing ingress blackbox probe (probe_success=0 and probe_http_status_code=0 for http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?..., where only the 'resolve' phase is recorded, 2-4 ms) is not evidence of an application fault: the direct hotel-reservation service probes (frontend:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, reservation:8087, search:8082, user:8086) all switch to probe_success=1 from 10:02-10:03Z and stay 1, so the application endpoints themselves were reachable.

Leading candidate: the `admin` user's readWrite privilege on geo-db was revoked by the script in ConfigMap failure-admin-geo (mounted at /scripts in mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-..., revision 2), so the geo service can no longer read geo-db. This would be invisible in request telemetry because geo does not issue per-request DB reads (all 4186 Nearby spans <=1 ms, mean 0.102 ms; mongodb-geo has the lowest mongod CPU), so the consequence would be silently degraded/empty geo results rather than errors; it would break as soon as geo has to read geo-db (restart, cold cache).

Second candidate: the same revocation applied to rate-db via ConfigMap failure-admin-rate; this can only be consistent if it was executed after the last observed rate->mongo access at 10:03:25.396Z, since every rate DB access before that succeeded and search reported zero failed calls.

The ~6% wrk2 socket timeouts (194/187/183/192 per 30 s round, 0 connect/read/write errors) represent requests that received no response at all, since every completed server span is under 10 ms and no non-2xx response was reported; a possible mechanism is a subset of requests hanging on a stale/blocked downstream gRPC connection, but no service could be tied to this with the available data.

Verify the actual MongoDB role state with a read-only query inside mongodb-geo (e.g. db.getUser('admin') on admin, checking the geo-db readWrite role) and, if it is missing, restore it with the already-mounted revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh; in parallel determine from the fault-runner's own record (not visible in this Run) whether revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh was executed and when.

gaps: No change-history/exec audit integration is available in this Run, and kubectl exec output is not written to pod stdout, so it cannot be observed whether, when, or on which mongod (geo or rate) revoke-admin-*-mongo.sh was executed; both candidate ConfigMaps were created and mounted by the same 10:01:5xZ release.

MongoDB user roles cannot be read: secrets are unreadable and no mongo client access is provided, so I could not verify directly whether `admin` still holds readWrite on geo-db / rate-db. MongoDB 4.4 does not log authorization failures by default, so absence of such lines is not evidence that a revocation did not happen.

The Kubernetes queries for Ingress objects (namespace hotel-reservation and cluster-wide) and for deployments in namespace ingress-nginx returned status no_data with zero items; since an empty result only means the query matched nothing in that view, I cannot assert whether an Ingress or ingress-nginx workload exists or existed, so the cause of the failing blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe remains unknown.

No baseline telemetry exists before the 10:01:50Z rollout of this app, so a latency/error comparison against a known-good period is impossible; the whole 24 h window contains only ~2.5 minutes of application life.

Jaeger retained only the newest traces (a 20-trace search at 10:04:17Z covered about one second at ~100 req/s), so long-hanging or earlier failed requests cannot be retrieved; error-tag searches for frontend, search and geo, duration>1 s searches for frontend, reservation, search and rate, and an otel.status_code=ERROR search for search all returned no_data, which limits any conclusion drawn from absent error spans.
The cause of wrk2's constant ~6% socket timeouts is unresolved: no server-side span, log line, status code or network counter (node_netstat_TcpExt_TCPTimeouts and softnet drops are 0) explains them.

The impact of the geo-db / rate-db privilege revocation hypotheses, including any degraded hotel/geo content returned to clients, could not be verified because response bodies are not observable; the load generator's byte counts (~1.2 MB per 30 s round, ~405 B per response) were the only content-related signal and no comparison baseline exists.

containers.name: archiver
command:
set -eu
record="${AUDIT_ARCHIVE_RECORD:-audit-archive-ready}"
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: starting audit log archive"
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: bundling /var/log/audit"
attempt=0
until reply=$(printf "%s\n" "$record" | nc -w 2 127.0.0.1 24224) && [ "$reply" = "$record" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  if [ "$attempt" -ge 10 ]; then
    echo "archiver: log forwarding unavailable" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 1
done
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: audit record forwarded"
sleep 1
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] archiver: upload complete (0 bytes archived); record=$record"

containers.name: fluent-bit-sidecar
command:
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] fluent-bit: binding to forward port 24224"
echo "[$(date -u '+%FT%TZ')] fluent-bit: ready to receive log streams"
exec nc -lk -p 24224 -e cat

data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
